# muxt test --output-cover-profile writes the template blocks the tests
# reached as a Go cover profile, and go tool cover -html opens it.
#
# The template file starts with its {{if}}, so the first reached span starts
# at the file's first byte: the profile counts line 1 from column 2, which
# is how x/tools' cover.Boundaries reads it. The test renders the admin
# branch only. The {{else}} branch is not in the profile, so go tool cover
# shows its text as not tracked: outside every span, neither covered nor
# uncovered.

muxt test --output-cover-profile cover.out
stdout '^ok  \tserver\t'
cmpenv cover.out want-cover.txt

exec go tool cover -html=cover.out -o out.html
grep '<span class="cov8" title="1">\{\{if \.Admin\}\}</span><span class="cov8" title="1">Welcome back, admin\.</span>\{\{else\}\}Please sign in\.<span' out.html
! grep '<span class="cov0" title' out.html

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- index.gohtml --
{{if .Admin}}Welcome back, admin.{{else}}Please sign in.{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Admin bool
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "index.gohtml", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestAdminPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Admin: true}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Welcome back, admin.\n"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}

mode: set

$WORK/index.gohtml:1.58,1.65 1 1
